name: admissible control set
definition: A_n is the set of controls admissible at update round n.
purpose: Separate the governed action space from the larger control universe.

name: purpose-feasible region
definition: F_n is the subset of currently admissible controls that can adequately serve stated purpose P from state x.
purpose: Detect the case where nominally large permission space has lost the controls that actually serve the assigned purpose.

name: contracting update
definition: A contracting update removes a neighborhood in response to observed boundary contact by a control used under the current regime.
purpose: Represent one direction of boundary learning without yet calling it a ratchet.

name: reopening update
definition: A reopening update restores a previously excluded region when evidence supports reversal, correction, or overconstraint.
purpose: Make expansion as representable and admissible to the dataset as contraction.

name: recursive dependence
definition: The next boundary is updated using evidence generated by behavior under the current boundary.
purpose: Identify history-dependent governance whose evidence and admissibility states are causally coupled.

name: pathological limit
definition: The limiting permitted space contains no control adequate to the stated purpose.
purpose: Operationalize the phrase safe because nothing can be done in it.

name: viability monotonicity at fixed state
formal: A_(n+1) subseteq A_n => K_j(t;A_(n+1)) subseteq K_j(t;A_n) => Gamma_t(x;A_(n+1)) subseteq Gamma_t(x;A_n)
definition: Holding state, target, dynamics, and disturbances fixed, contraction of admissible controls cannot create a control strategy unavailable under the larger set.
purpose: Connect the boundary mechanism to the existing viable-set notation without comparing different realized states as if they were identical.

name: ratchet classification
formal: sequential contraction + history dependence + reopening evaluated + no observed reopening under qualifying correction evidence
definition: A ratchet classification requires a sequence, not an isolated restriction, and cannot be assigned until bidirectional correction has been tested.
purpose: Prevent the dataset from treating every safety boundary or every tightening as recursively contracting.

name: adaptive boundary classification
formal: evidence can produce both contraction and purpose-relevant reopening
definition: An adaptive boundary is evidenced when qualifying observations can shrink and later restore useful admissible action space.
purpose: Give positive evidence against a one-way ratchet interpretation full standing.
